UI_MultiTow_Description: Settings for the Multi-Vehicle Towing mod. Changes apply immediately; existing trains stay connected. In multiplayer the server's sandbox options decide the rules; sounds, link display, remarks and the train display stay personal.
UI_MultiTow_JavaNote: MULTITOW_JAVANOTE:Options in red need ZombieBuddy (Java part). Without it they have no effect - the mod runs in basic mode.
UI_MultiTow_Enabled_tt: Off = the game works exactly like vanilla (one trailer or one towed vehicle only).
UI_MultiTow_RequireHook: Require Heavy Chain Hook from the 3rd vehicle on
UI_MultiTow_RequireHook_tt: When on, coupling a third or further vehicle uses up one Heavy Chain Hook from your inventory. Detaching gives it back; if the link snaps while driving, a Heavy Chain and a Large Hook drop on the ground. Coupling two vehicles stays free.
UI_MultiTow_Sounds_tt: Plays chain sounds when coupling, detaching and when a link snaps.
UI_MultiTow_ShowChains_tt: Draws the chain or tow bar between coupled vehicles. A loose chain sags. Only a picture: it is drawn on top of the vehicles. Personal setting.
UI_MultiTow_HazardStyle_tt: How the hazard lights of towed vehicles look. They blink at the front and the rear. American = red at the rear (tail and brake lights plus a red light), orange at the front. European = orange at the front and the rear. The blinking lights tint the ground and the vehicle (best seen at dusk and night; the game has no orange lamps on the vehicle models). Switch them on and off in the vehicle radial menu (V) as driver of the towing vehicle.
UI_MultiTow_HazardScope_tt: Only the last vehicle of the train, or every towed vehicle.
UI_MultiTow_ShowLinks_tt: Draws every link between two vehicles as a band. Green = relaxed, yellow = under load, red = close to snapping. Only visible to you.
UI_MultiTow_LinkKey_tt: Key that shows the link stress bands. Works even when the option above is off.
UI_MultiTow_LinkKeyMode_tt: Hold = the bands are visible while the key is held down. Toggle = one press turns them on, the next press turns them off.
UI_MultiTow_ShowLinksNear_tt: When you are on foot within about 2 m of a link between two vehicles, its band is shown automatically.
UI_MultiTow_Remarks_tt: Your character comments on the train after coupling. With a vehicle limit the remarks get more strained the closer you get to it; without a limit they get more sarcastic the longer the train gets.
UI_MultiTow_SpeedUnit_tt: Unit for the speed limit below. Only the speed slider of the selected unit can be changed.
UI_MultiTow_ShowSetup: Show setup assistant on next start
UI_MultiTow_ShowSetup_tt: Shows the setup assistant again the next time you are in the main menu. It walks through all options page by page.
UI_MultiTow_DebugZBWarning: Show ZombieBuddy warning in setup assistant
UI_MultiTow_DebugZBWarning_tt: For testing. Opens the setup assistant the next time you are in the main menu and shows the warning page 'ZombieBuddy is not active' even if ZombieBuddy works. Switches itself off when you finish or skip the assistant.
UI_MultiTow_ShowDebug_tt: Shows the options below. They are meant for testing and troubleshooting.
UI_MultiTow_DebugRedOptions: Mark options that need ZombieBuddy in red
UI_MultiTow_DebugRedOptions_tt: Preview: shows the options that need ZombieBuddy in red, as players without ZombieBuddy see them. The hint line at the top of General appears the next time the options are opened.
UI_MultiTow_DebugHostServerJava: Host games: start ZombieBuddy on the hosted server (test)
UI_MultiTow_DebugHostServerJava_tt: Only for games started with Host. The game starts its own background server for them, but without ZombieBuddy - so that server has no Java part and chains are off for everybody. With this option the background server also starts with ZombieBuddy (and all Java mods you already allowed permanently; it cannot ask you, so new or changed JARs are skipped). Takes effect the next time you click Host. Experimental: switch it off if hosting fails.
UI_MultiTow_SetupWelcome: Welcome! This assistant appears once and lets you set up the mod before your first drive. Go through the pages with Next and confirm at the end. Everything can be changed later under Options > DO Utilities.
UI_MultiTow_SetupKeyHint: change it in Options > DO Utilities
UI_MultiTow_SetupInfo: Point at an option to see what it does.
UI_MultiTow_SetupZBIntro: The Java part of this mod (MultiTowCore.jar) was not loaded. Only the game's normal towing works (one towed vehicle). Without ZombieBuddy there are:
UI_MultiTow_SetupZBLost1: No trains with 3 or more vehicles
UI_MultiTow_SetupZBLost2: No rigid tow bar link (the tow bar is only an item)
UI_MultiTow_SetupZBLost3: No extra engine power, no train brake, no speed limit
UI_MultiTow_SetupZBLost4: No visible chains and tow bars, no link stress display
UI_MultiTow_SetupZBLost5: No link wear and no hazard lights on towed vehicles
UI_MultiTow_SetupZBLost6: Multiplayer: coupling with this mod is switched off
UI_MultiTow_SetupZBFix: How to fix: install ZombieBuddy, start the game with it and allow MultiTowCore.jar when ZombieBuddy asks. You can still go through the setup now.
UI_MultiTow_Wear_tt: Links wear out while driving, faster under heavy load. Chains wear about three times faster than tow bars. At 0 %% the link snaps. A tow bar keeps its condition when detached; real trailers do not wear. A worn tow bar can be repaired: right-click it, Repair (blowtorch, Welding 2, small sheet metal or 2 scrap metal).
UI_MultiTow_Cargo_tt: How much of the cargo (everything in trunks, seats and glove boxes) adds to the weight of vehicles in a train. Heavier vehicles pull harder on the links and brake and accelerate more slowly. Off = the game's own calculation, which only updates when the vehicle is loaded.
UI_MultiTow_HazardAuto_tt: Coupling a vehicle switches on the hazard lights of the train. They can be switched off in the vehicle radial menu (V).
UI_MultiTow_Assist_tt: A towed vehicle with its engine running drives along when the towing vehicle accelerates, with this share of its own engine power. 0 = off. Only available when the extra engine power of the towing vehicle is Off for cars AND trucks/vans (both settings below).
UI_MultiTow_Hud_tt: A small window with information about the train. Visible while you sit in a vehicle that is part of a train.
UI_MultiTow_HudPos_tt: Free = drag the window with the mouse, the position is remembered. Otherwise it sits at a corner or side of the screen.
UI_MultiTow_HudShowCount_tt: Number of vehicles in the train, and the limit if one is set.
UI_MultiTow_HudShowSpeed_tt: Current speed, and the speed limit if one is set (in the unit chosen above).
UI_MultiTow_HudShowStress_tt: The most strained link as a bar from green to red, with its number (#1 = first link behind the towing vehicle).
UI_MultiTow_HudShowCond_tt: The most worn link (only when wear is on). At 0 %% it snaps.
UI_MultiTow_HudShowWeight_tt: Total weight of the train, including the part of the cargo set under Gameplay.
UI_MultiTow_HudShowFuel_tt: Fuel of the towing vehicle and the extra fuel use of the train.
UI_MultiTow_SectionCarHint: Applies to trains whose towing vehicle (the first vehicle) is a car, SUV or similar.
UI_MultiTow_SectionTruckHint: Applies to trains whose towing vehicle (the first vehicle) is a pickup, van, step van, truck or ambulance.
UI_MultiTow_MaxVehicles_tt: Counts all vehicles in the train including the towing vehicle. Decided by the type of the towing vehicle. Trains that are already coupled are never split by lowering this value.
UI_MultiTow_BoostFactor_tt: Off = no extra power. Fixed factors multiply the engine force of the towing vehicle. Automatic grows with every additional towed vehicle. Only applies when more than one vehicle is towed.
UI_MultiTow_Brake_tt: How hard the towed vehicles brake along when the towing vehicle brakes. 0 = they don't brake (vanilla), 100 = as hard as if someone were braking in each of them.
UI_MultiTow_Speed_tt: Top speed for trains with 3 or more vehicles. Above it the engine gets no more throttle; well above it the towing vehicle brakes gently. 0 = no limit.
UI_MultiTow_FuelMode_tt: Extra fuel used by the towing vehicle from the 3rd vehicle on. Even = the percentage below is added once per additional vehicle. Exponential = the extra use grows faster with every additional vehicle.
UI_MultiTow_FuelPercent_tt: Example with 20 %% and 4 towed vehicles: Even = 1.6x fuel use, Exponential = 1.73x.
UI_MultiTow_Noise_tt: A moving train makes noise at every link that attracts zombies. Chains are loud, tow bars much quieter. The faster you drive, the farther it carries.
UI_MultiTow_JavaMissing: Multi-Tow: basic mode - ZombieBuddy is not active
UI_MultiTow_JavaRestartNote: Restart needed: Multi-Vehicle Towing was switched on while the game was running. ZombieBuddy has loaded the Java part, but it only works after a restart. Please quit the game and start it again - until then the options in red have no effect.
UI_MultiTow_JavaRestart: Multi-Tow: please restart the game - the Java part was loaded while the game was running
UI_MultiTow_SetupRestartIntro: This mod was switched on while the game was running. ZombieBuddy has already loaded the Java part (MultiTowCore.jar), but the game can only use it after a restart. Until then only the game's normal towing works (one towed vehicle), and there are:
UI_MultiTow_SetupRestartFix: How to fix: quit the game completely and start it again. Nothing else is needed. You can still go through the setup now.
UI_MultiTow_ServerJavaMissing: Multi-Tow: the server has no Java part - chains are disabled
UI_MultiTow_TooLong: Multi-Tow: the train is already at its maximum length
